slides.title: The stopping condition
slides.narration: The ball is dropped from a height of 8 metres. We count distance until it reaches the ground for the fifth time.

slides.title: Four rebound heights
slides.caption: h_k=8\left(\frac34\right)^k
slides.narration: After the first contact, the ball rises to six metres. Each later rebound is three-fourths of the previous one, and only four rebound heights occur before the fifth contact.

slides.title: Count each journey
slides.caption: D=8+2(h_1+h_2+h_3+h_4)
slides.narration: The initial eight-metre drop happens only once. Each rebound height is traveled twice: once going up and once coming back down.

slides.title: The finite sum
slides.caption: h_1+h_2+h_3+h_4=6+\frac92+\frac{27}{8}+\frac{81}{32}
slides.narration: The rebound heights form a finite geometric series: six, then nine-halves, then twenty-seven-eighths, then eighty-one-thirty-seconds.

slides.title: Use the geometric formula
slides.caption: S_n=a\frac{1-r^n}{1-r}
slides.narration: For a finite geometric series, the sum is a times one minus r to the n, divided by one minus r. Here, a is six metres, r is three-fourths, and n is four.

slides.title: Substitute the sum
slides.caption: D=8+2\left[6\frac{1-\left(\frac34\right)^4}{1-\frac34}\right]
slides.narration: Substitute the geometric-series sum into the distance formula. The initial drop remains eight metres, and the rebound sum is still doubled.

slides.title: Evaluate the distance
slides.caption: D=\frac{653}{16}\text{ m}=40.8125\text{ m}
slides.narration: Adding the four rebound heights, counting each twice, and then adding the initial drop gives an exact total of six hundred fifty-three sixteenths metres, or 40.8125 metres.

slides.title: FINAL ANSWER
slides.caption: D=40.8125\text{ m}=40\frac{13}{16}\text{ m}
slides.narration: Therefore, before the ball reaches the ground for the fifth time, it travels 40.8125 metres in total, which is also 40 and 13 sixteenths metres.
